evidence.note: Ran enumerated end-to-end feature sweeps and explicitly listed done-vs-remaining across all subsystems plus fine-grained contract items (EntityTooSmall, ETag format, versioning/tagging), demonstrating a usable, granular checklist.
Repeated the same failing heredoc-append approach ~10 times, corrupting main.py again and again before recognizing the pattern and switching strategy — slow to detect a stuck loop.

Long circular-debug stretch on multipart completion, cycling through several wrong root-cause hypotheses; eventually named the namespace impasse, showing partial stuck-recognition rather than early recognition.

Server went silent/possibly crashed and step 144 acknowledges 'several known bugs to fix,' yet the agent submitted 'complete' three times without verifying — a horizon-level coverage-tracking failure, and its bug list contradicted the earlier abort-routing fix (step 138).

reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds the level-5 anchor: it kept a usable running checklist of subsystems AND tracked specific contract items (error codes, ETag rule, testids), knowing generally what remained. But it falls short of level-8: it looped repeatedly on file corruption and multipart without early stuck-recognition, and at the horizon it lost situational awareness — submitting 'complete' three times against a silent server and its own list of unresolved known bugs, with tracking that had become internally inconsistent. That mix of genuine granular tracking undercut by late thrashing and a degraded end-state picture places it at a 6.
